newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes extend gains late, talk thins.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes extend gains late, talk thins.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices continued rising late, following the lead of heating oil, which saw news highs amid thin local trade.
Differentials for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude were unchanged with many traders out of the market for an industry function.
Outright prices for Alaskan grade rose 80 cents to $22.40/22.70 a barrel, in line with November West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
Benchmark WTI tracked heating oil, which hit a high of 74.80 in intraday trade.
Buyers kept bids at $2.50 on Thursday and said business was quiet as they evaluated positions.
One buyer saw increased imports of Oriente adding pressure to diffs. A major producer offered at $2.10 under November WTI.
Line 63 remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, was unchanged at $16.15/16.35 a barrel.
And prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude held at $17.60/17.70.
